entities.summary: Pope Miltiades, also known as Melchiades the African, was the bishop of Rome from 311 to his death on 10 or 11 January 314. It was during his pontificate that Emperor Constantine the Great issued the Edict of Milan (313), giving Christianity legal status within the Roman Empire. The pope also received the palace of Empress Fausta where the Lateran Palace, the papal seat and residence of the papal administration, would be built. At the Lateran Council, during the schism with the Church of Carthage, Miltiades condemned the rebaptism of apostatised bishops and priests, a teaching of Donatus Magnus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Miltiades played a crucial role in establishing Christianity as a legal religion within the Roman Empire, paving the way for its spread across Europe. The Edict of Milan issued during his pontificate granted tolerance to Christians, marking a significant turning point in the history of Christianity.
